ablate: To remove or decrease something by cutting, erosion, melting, evaporation, or vaporization.
To undergo ablation; to become melted or evaporated and removed at a high temperature.
ablative absolute: A construction in Latin and other sister languages in which an independent phrase with a noun in the ablative case has a participle, adjective, or noun, expressed or implied, which agrees with it in gender, number and case – both words forming a clause grammatically unconnected with the rest of the sentence.
able seaman: A seaman, especially one in the merchant navy, who has been trained or certified in all routine duties; a member of the Royal Navy rated between ordinary seaman and leading seaman or boatswain's mate.
able-bodied: Having a sound, strong body; physically competent; robust; fit for service.
Not disabled; having no physical disability.
Capable of performing all requisite duties as a seaman, specifically in the Royal Navy, a rating between leading and ordinary.
ableist: One who exhibits ableism, or prejudice against the disabled.
abloom: In or into bloom; in a blooming state; having flower blooms unfolding.
Thriving in health, beauty, and vigor; exhibiting youth-like beauty.
ablution block: A simple structure with toilets, showers, and wash basins, for communal use, as at a camping ground, caravan park, etc.
ably: In an able manner; with great ability.
abnegation: A denial; a renunciation; denial of desire or self-interest.
abnormal hieratic: The highly simplified and cursive ancient Egyptian script that developed from Upper Egyptian hieratic writing from around 1100 BCE until its supersession by its Lower Egyptian counterpart Demotic around 650 BCE.
abnormal psychology: The academic study of persons whose psychological characteristics deviate from the norm, such as neuroses, psychoses, and other disorders.
An instance of a person having psychological characteristics that deviate from the norm.
abnormally: In an abnormal manner; in a way that deviates from a standard, norm, or average.
abo group: The basic system of categorizing blood by antigen type.
abominably: In an abominable manner; very odiously; detestably.
aboot: In a circle around; all round; on every side of; on the outside of; around.
aboriginal american: A member or descendant of the first immigrants to North America.
Of the original settlers of North America.
aboriginal english: A variety of English spoken by Indigenous Australians.
aborning: That is in the process of being born; coming into existence; before coming to completion.
abortion clinic: A clinic where abortions are performed.
abortion pill: A drug, such as mifepristone (Mifegyne), used to terminate a pregnancy in its earliest stage.
abortion tourism: Travel for the purpose of obtaining an abortion where it is legal.
abortion tourist: Someone who travels for the purpose of obtaining an abortion where it is legal.
abortion vaccine: A vaccine which prevents certain diseases known to cause spontaneous abortion in livestock.
abortionist: A person who performs abortions, especially illegally or secretly.
A person who advocates for or supports the legality of abortion.
abound in one's own sense: To follow one’s own inclinations and opinions.
about box: A window displaying information about an application, such as its version number and copyright or other licence.
about east: OK; all right; in a proper manner.
about me: Synonym of bio (“a section of a user profile that contains information about the user”).
about one's ears: In close proximity to one; near at hand.
about page: a type of web page commonly seen on websites, containing general information about the person or organization that is responsible for the website in question, usually a description of the site's history and mission or purpose.
about ship: Tack; to cause to turn into the wind and through the other side ending with a full 180 degree turn.
about sledge: The largest hammer used by smiths.
A warning that the heavy about sledge is about to be swung, usually by a hammerman.
about that life: Having or desiring an ostentatious lifestyle, especially involving sex, drugs, and violence.
about you: Synonym of bio (“a field within a form of an online user profile that is meant to be filled out with information about the user”).
above and beyond: Further than; doing more than is expected or required.
Doing more than is expected or required.
above ground: On or above the surface of the ground.
Not of or relating to the social or political underground; in the open; existing within or produced by the establishment.
above one's huckleberry: Synonym of above one's bend (“beyond one's power or ability”).
above one's station: Of higher social status than suitable for one's position, standing, or rank.
above oneself: Acting with an undue opinion of one's own importance or abilities.
Acting without inhibition due to high spirits.
above par: Better than the average or normal standard.
Having a price below its face value.
(of a score) More than par for the hole or course.
above proof: Overproof; containing more alcohol than proof spirit.
above stairs: In or pertaining to the part of a large house, typically the above-ground rooms, in which the owning family lives, contrasted with below stairs where the servants are accommodated.
above the curve: With above average innovative performance or quality, especially a trailblazer developing advances before competitors.
above the fold: By extension, situated near the top of a web page or application screen; not requiring scrolling. See above the scroll.
Occupying an exclusive position of relative prominence
Situated in the upper half of the front page of a broadsheet newspaper, and thus more prominent, as the lower half is not usually visible when the folded newspaper is displayed for sale.
above the fray: Uninvolved in a difficult argument or struggle.
having an affectedly nonchalant or mature attitude about a dispute seen as petty.
above the line: In the part of the score sheet in bridge that is reserved for honors, penalty, and premiums; a score that does not count towards game.
Classified as an ordinary expense or revenue item, or a current asset.
Having a broad reach rather than targeting a specific demographic.
Who guide and influence the creative direction, process, and voice of a given narrative in a film, such as the screenwriter, producer, director, and actors.
above the neck rule: A guideline for deciding whether to exercise when sick, which posits that if symptoms (like a runny nose, sneezing, or mild sore throat) are only "above the neck," light to moderate activity may be permissible, but "below the neck" symptoms (chest congestion, body aches, cough) indicate one should refrain from exercise to avoid worsening illness.
above the rim: at a high level of excellence
[handing the ball] higher than the rim of the basket (such as during a slam dunk or alley oop)
above the table: Outside the fictional reality of the game; in real life.
aboveboard: In open sight; without trick, concealment, or deception.
aboveground: On or above the surface of the ground.
archbishop: A senior bishop who is in charge of an archdiocese, and presides over a group of dioceses called a province (in Catholicism, Eastern Orthodoxy, Anglicanism, etc.)
abridge: To make shorter; to shorten in duration or extent.
abridged: Cut or shortened, especially of a literary work.
abrader: Something that abrades; a tool or machine for abrading.
A primitive artifact made of sandstone used for smoothing, sharpening, or shaping.
A surgical instrument used to abrade bone or other tissue.
abraham man: Any beggar who pretends to be ill, physically or mentally, to obtain alms.
abraham's bosom: The waiting place for the faithful dead between the crucifixion and the resurrection of Christ; paradise.
abrasion platform: A sloping or nearly flat bedrock surface extending out from the foot of a marine cliff under shallow water of a breaker (wave) zone, that was created by marine abrasion.
abrasive disc: A disc of abrasive material that rotates in a tool such as a sander.
abrasiveness: The property, quality or instance of being abrasive.
abraxas: Mystical word of Gnostic origins that carries many meanings, including as a proper name.

A theonym of unclear signification, commonly invoked as a magic word on amulets, talismans, and papyri in the Mediterranean basin from the 2nd century B.C. until the 13th century, and viewed in Gnosticism as one of the Archons who follows Sabaoth when he leaves the ranks of the Demiurge to become an aeon alongside Sophia.
abridgement: The act of abridging; reduction or deprivation
abridgment: The act of abridging; reduction or deprivation
The state of being abridged or lessened.
An epitome or compend, as of a book; a shortened or abridged form; an abbreviation.
The leaving out of certain portions of a plaintiff's demand, the writ still holding good for the remainder.
abrogation: The blocking of a molecular process or function.
abruptness: The state of being abrupt or broken
absent: Being away from a place; withdrawn from a place; existing but not present; (sometimes) missing.
absolute: Free of restrictions, limitations, qualifications or conditions; unconditional.
abstract: An abridgement or summary of a longer publication.
absolutely: In an absolute or unconditional manner; utterly, positively, wholly.
abscise: To separate by means of abscission; to shed or drop off.
abscisic: Of or pertaining to abscisic acid or its derivatives.
abscisic acid: A terpenoid best known as a plant hormone that inhibits seed germination and was once thought to be important in abscission.
abscission: The act or process of cutting off.
The natural separation of a part at a predetermined location, such as a leaf at the base of the petiole.
A figure of speech employed when a speaker having begun to say a thing stops abruptly
abscission layer: A layer of cells in a plant that differ from those above and below, and contain abundant starch and dense cytoplasm, which upon disorganization, begin the process of abscission, or the natural separation of the leaf from the rest of the plant.
abscission zone: The area in a plant's leaf, stem, or fruit stalk, where the abscission layer if formed along with weakened sclerenchyma, absent collenchyma, and dense cytoplasm.
abseil: To descend a steep or vertical drop using a rope with a mechanical friction device or (classic abseil) by wrapping the rope around the body.
A descent in mountaineering using a rope looped at the top and a friction device.
absence makes the heart go yonder: Synonym of long absent, soon forgotten (“separation can result in someone finding other emotional attachments”)
absence makes the heart grow fonder: One feels more love or affection for those one loves when parted from them.
absence of mind: A state or the quality of being absent-minded (abstracted, preoccupied).
absence seizure: A type of seizure indicative of petit mal epilepsy, usually lasting up to thirty seconds and involving vacantness and lack of awareness, possibly including twitching; not including spasm or unconsciousness.
absence without leave: The military offense of not being present when expected without proper authority.
absent over leave: Failing to return from leave or liberty on time.
absent treatment: Interpersonal treatment (way of interacting), usually mistreatment, that ignores the presence of a person.
absent without leave: In the armed forces, being absent from one's post without prior authorization.
absentee ballot: A vote made remotely, especially a postal vote, cast by a voter unable to be present in person.
absentee vote: A vote cast by a voter by mail because of absence from the precinct during the election, typically military members.
absentee voter: A registered voter who is permitted to vote by absentee ballot, due to absence from district during the election.
absentee voting: Any of several methods of allowing people to vote without attending an official voting station
absenteeism: The state of being absent, especially frequently or without good reason; the practice of an absentee.
The practice of absenting oneself from the country or district where one's estate is situated.
absently: In an absent-minded or abstracted manner.
absentminded: Absent in mind; often preoccupied; forgetful or careless due to distraction; easily distracted.
absinth: The herb absinthium Artemisia absinthium (grande wormwood); essence of wormwood.
absinthe oil: A dark green narcotic oil derived from wormwood and used in liqueurs; wormwood oil.
absolute address: A numerical value that identifies a fixed location in real storage in terms of the number of bytes from the beginning, or in a peripheral device in terms of disks, sectors and bytes.
absolute advantage: The capability to produce more of a given product using the same quantity or less of a given resource than a competing entity.
absolute alcohol: Reasonably pure ethyl alcohol that contains at most 1% of water
absolute altitude: The vertical distance between the airplane and the surface below.
absolute assembler: An assembler that generates code that uses only absolute addresses.
absolute blocking: A system of managing trains that breaks the line into small segments, and if a train is in a segment, no other train may follow, unless the second train is following the first, with caution.
absolute ceiling: The maximum altitude above sea level that an aircraft or missile can maintain horizontal flight under normal conditions.
absolute cinema: Any event or work personally considered to be outstanding or amusing.
Cinema that is personally considered to be outstanding.
absolute code: Code which uses only absolute addresses.
absolute complement: The set that contains exactly those elements belonging to the universal set but not to a given set.
absolute constant: A constant that maintains the same value wherever it occurs; such as π.
absolute deviation: The shortest distance between the center of the target and the point where the projectile hit or burst.
The absolute value of the difference between a given value (such as mean or expected value) and a variate value (usually an observed value).
absolute differential calculus: Ricci calculus; the rules of index notation and manipulation for tensors and tensor fields, as developed by Gregorio Ricci-Curbastro.
absolute ego: The Fichtean ego that posits its own existence and through the opposition of subject and object thus created dialectically evolves the universe.
absolute error: Shortest distance between the center of impact or the center of burst of a group of shots, and the point of impact or burst of a single shot within the group.
Error of a sight consisting of its error in relation to a master service sight with which it is tested, including the known error of the master service sight.
The difference (sometimes defined to be the absolute difference) between the measured or inferred value of a quantity and its true value.
absolute form: The Platonic form of the supreme idea in which all other ideas participate.
absolute frequency: the number of data points satisfying something
absolute geometry: The single (up to logical equivalence) geometry whose axiomatic system is equivalent to that of Euclidean geometry without the parallel postulate or any alternative.
Any geometry whose axiomatic system extends that of absolute geometry (in the singular sense) and neither assumes nor contradicts the parallel postulate.
absolute humidity: In a system of moist air, the ratio of the mass of water vapor present to the volume occupied by the mixture, that is, the density of the water vapor component. Absolute humidity is usually expressed in grams of water vapor per cubic meter or, in engineering practice, in grains per cubic foot. Because this measure of atmospheric humidity is not conservative with respect to adiabatic expansion or compression, it is not commonly used by meteorologists. (Also called vapor concentration and vapor density). See relative humidity.
absolute idea: In Hegelianism, the spiritual principle of which the reality is the expression.
absolute immunity: A doctrine providing immunity from suit by private parties for certain government officials and witnesses in judicial proceedings, even if the act or testimony was illegal, false, or made in bad faith.
absolute impediment: A diriment impediment that prevents a person from marrying, but does not require punishment or an annulment.
absolute loader: A loader that places absolute code into main memory beginning with the initial address assigned by the assembler. No address manipulation is performed.
absolute magnitude: The intrinsic luminosity that a celestial body would have if viewed from a distance of 10 parsecs or about 32.6 light years.
absolute monarch: The ruler of an absolute monarchy.
absolute monarchy: The rule of such a monarch, as a form of government.
A state over which a sole monarch has absolute and unlimited power.
absolute music: Instrumental music having an intellectual and affective content, which depends solely on its rhythmic, melodic, and contrapuntal structure.
absolute path: A path or address that identifies a file or web page which includes all the information necessary to find the file or web page with no assumptions based on local context.
absolute pitch: The exact pitch of a note as established by its rate of vibration based on a standard scale.
Perfect pitch; the ability to identify or produce any tone without need of an external reference.
absolute pressure: Total pressure in a fluid equivalent to the sum of the gage and the atmospheric pressures.
absolute reality: Ultimate reality, as is unaffected by the beliefs or limitations of any finite being.
Reality in relation to the divine mind.
absolute scale: A temperature scale whose zero corresponds to absolute zero such as the Kelvin scale or Rankine scale.
absolute skewer: A skewer in which the king is placed in check, forcing it to be moved.
absolute space: The Newtonian concept of an unchanging and unchangeable reference system of spatial (and temporal) coordinates that is the same for all observers
absolute state: A state with absolute sovereignty and authority, in contrast with e.g. a feudal state.
To denote the only state not construct state as in the binary state system of Ugaritic.
Denotes the indeterminate state in Aramaic, even though it also has a determinate state called emphatic state.

Denotes an infrequent endingless state in Akkadian used for predicative sentences, adverbially used nouns and vocative expressions (in which cases Arabic would use the accusative case), contrasting with the governed state and the construct state.
absolute superlative: In Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, and Catalan: the form of an adjective formed by adding the suffixes -issimo, -ísimo, -íssimo, -érrimo, -imo, or -íssim to the adjective (with any final vowel dropped) to express a superlative that cannot be exceeded, having the sense “as ... as possible”.

In Greek: one of the degrees of comparison in an adjective that stresses an exceptional property without making a direct comparison, its closest equivalent in English being a most important letter, a very high mountain or absolutely pure water. It is formed by adding the suffix -τατος (declined) to the adjective's nominative, neuter singular.

In Romanian: a form of an adjective with various adverbs preceding it: foarte / tare / extrem de / cât se poate de + adjective. The most frequent and standard adverb is foarte (“very”). The other adverbs or adverbial constructions are emotionally marked. The adverb tare is used in the colloquial style.
absolute system: The system of measurements based on force, and independent of acceleration of gravity.
absolute territory: The area of bare skin above the top of above-the-knee socks but below the hemline of a miniskirt or pair of shorts.
absolute time: The Newtonian concept of an unchanging and unchangeable reference system of time (and spatial) coordinates that is the same for all observers.
absolute unit: Anything exceptionally large for its type.
A unit of measurement that can be defined in terms of mass, length, and time.
An exceptionally large or stout person.
absolutely convergent: Of an infinite series, convergent even if the absolute value is taken of each term; a stronger condition than ordinary convergence.
absolutely flat: Synonym of regular (“a von Neumann regular”).
absolution: An absolving of sins from ecclesiastical penalties by an authority.
The forgiveness of sins, in a general sense.
The form of words by which a penitent is absolved.
An absolving, or setting free from guilt, sin, or penalty; forgiveness of an offense.
absolutive: Of or pertaining to the grammatical case prototypically used to indicate the sole argument of an intransitive verb, and the more patientive argument of a transitive verb.
The absolutive case, or a phrase that uses it.
An uninflected verb form used to indicate another action performed by the subject of the principal verb.
Of, exhibiting, or pertaining to absolution; absolutory, absolving.
absolve: To set free, release or discharge (from obligations, debts, responsibility etc.).
To pronounce free from or give absolution for a penalty, blame, or guilt.
To pronounce not guilty; to grant a pardon for.
To grant a remission of sin; to give absolution to.
absorb oneself in: To become preoccupied by (some topic or activity).
absorbance: A logarithmic measure of the amount of light that is absorbed when passing through a substance; the capacity of a substance to absorb light of a given wavelength; optical density.
absorbed dose: The amount of energy imparted by nuclear (or ionizing) radiation to unit mass of absorbing material. Units of measure include the gray, the rad, and their derivatives (e.g., centigray, millirad).
absorbedly: In a manner as if wholly engrossed or engaged.
absorbency: The ratio of the absorbance or optical density of a substance to that of a similar body of pure solvent.
absorbent cotton: Cotton which has had its fatty matter removed to become capable of absorbing liquids; cotton wool.
absorber: A device which causes gas or vapor to be absorbed by a liquid.
A material that absorbs neutrons in a reactor.
absorbing: Allowing a process to enter it, but not to leave it.
absorption band: One of any number of ranges of wavelengths of electromagnetic radiation absorbed by a substance.
absorption coefficient: A measure of the absorption of electromagnetic radiation as it passes through a specific substance; the fraction of incident radiation absorbed by unit mass or unit thickness; absorptivity.
absorption edge: The boundary of a dark band in an x-ray spectrum.
absorption factor: The measurement of a specific substance's ability to absorb radiant energy; absorptivity.
absorption line: A spectral line that corresponds to the absorption of electromagnetic radiation at a specific wavelength; the pattern of such lines is characteristic of specific atoms or molecules in the path of the radiation.
absorption refrigerator: A refrigeration system that drives its cooling effect using energy provided by a heat source, specifically by making a coolant (often water or ammonia) evaporate and be absorbed into another substance (often lithium bromide or water, respectively) before the two substances are again separated by heating.
absorption spectroscopy: A form of spectroscopy that analysis absorption spectrums.
absorption spectrum: The characteristic pattern of dark lines or bands that occurs when electromagnetic radiation is passed through an absorbing medium into a spectroscope.
absorption system: A refrigeration system that drives its cooling effect using energy provided by a heat source, specifically by making a coolant (often water or ammonia) evaporate and be absorbed into another substance (often lithium bromide or water, respectively) before the two substances are again separated by heating.
absorptive: Having power, capacity, or tendency to absorb or imbibe; absorbent.
absquatulate: To leave quickly or in a hurry; to depart, flee.
abstainer: One who abstains; especially, one who abstains from something, such as the use of alcohol or drugs, or one who abstains for religious reasons; one who practices self-denial.
abstemious: Refraining from freely consuming food or strong drink; sparing in diet; abstinent, temperate.
Sparing in the indulgence of the appetite or passions.
Sparingly used; used with temperance or moderation.
Marked by, or spent in, abstinence.
abstinence only: A form of sex education that advocates only abstinence as a means to avoid pregnancy and sexually transmitted diseases.
abstinence syndrome: The physical symptoms of an addict who is withdrawing; withdrawal.
abstinent: Refraining from indulgence, especially from the indulgence of appetite.
One of a Christian sect that appeared in France and Spain in the 3rd century, and practised abstinence from meat and sex.
abstract: An abridgement or summary of a longer publication.
abstracted: Separated or disconnected; withdrawn; removed; apart.
abstract analytic number theory: A branch of number theory in which suitable ideas and techniques from analytic number theory are generalised and applied to a variety of mathematical fields.
abstract art: Art that does not depict objects in the natural world, but instead uses color and form in a non-representational way.
abstract away from: To omit the consideration of details regarding (something); to dismiss the details of (something) so as to concern oneself with higher features and more complex/interesting elements.
abstract class: A class that cannot be instantiated and may have abstract method.
abstract data type: A data type defined only by data properties and operations to be performed on the data without any specification as to how the data will be represented or the operations performed.
abstract expressionism: An American genre of modern art that used improvised techniques, such as sinuous linearity, to generate highly abstract forms while allowing the artist spontaneity.
abstract expressionist: An artist who works within the genre of Abstract Expressionism.
abstract factory class: A class that has an abstract method to create an object.
abstract factory pattern: A creational design pattern that decouples the object creation by providing a group of individual factories by defining an abstract factory class.
abstract harmonic analysis: A branch of harmonic analysis dealing with generalised Fourier transforms that act on functions defined on Hausdorff locally compact topological groups.
abstract idea: An idea separated from a complex object, or from other ideas which naturally accompany it; as the solidity of marble when contemplated apart from its color or figure.
abstract language: Words that represent concepts rather than physical things
abstract method: A method of an abstract class that has no implementation in that class and must therefore be implemented by all subtyping classes.
abstract model: A model that contains an abstraction or abstractions of the reality.
abstract nonsense: Details which are straightforward but so tedious that an author or lecturer would rather skip them (especially those of a category theoretical nature).
abstract number: A number used without application to things, e.g. 6, 8, 10; but when applied to anything, e.g. 6 feet, 10 men, it becomes concrete.
abstract of title: An epitome of the evidences of ownership; the condensed history of title to a particular parcel of real estate, with encumbrances.
abstract publication: A scientific publication which concentrates on publishing abstracts of scientific writings.
abstract term: A term expressing an abstract idea, such as beauty, whiteness, or roundness, without indicating any object in which it exists.
A name for an order, genera, or species of things in which there is a combination of similar qualities.
abstract type: a type in a nominative type system that cannot be instantiated.
abstracted: Separated or disconnected; withdrawn; removed; apart.
Inattentive to surrounding objects; absent in mind; meditative.
abstractedly: In an abstracted manner; separately; in the abstract.
abstractionist: Related or tending to abstractionism, particularly art.
Someone who supports or creates abstract art.
abstractive: Having an abstracting nature or tendency; tending to separate; tending to be withdrawn.
Derived by abstraction; belonging to abstraction.
abstractly: In an abstract way or manner
absurdist: An advocate of absurdism, in particular a writer of absurd topics.
absurdity: That which is absurd; an absurd action; a logical contradiction.
The quality of being absurd or inconsistent with obvious truth, reason, or sound judgment.
abt: all but thesis: The status of a master's degree, doctoral, or (infrequently) undergraduate student who has completed all degree requirements except the culminating thesis.
about: In a circle around; all round; on every side of; on the outside of; around.
In a circle around; all round; on every side of; on the outside of; around.
abundance of caution: Caution used to justify preemptive measures that are likely not strictly necessary.
abundant number: A number that is less than the sum of its proper divisors (all divisors except the number itself).
abuse of notation: The use of a mathematical notation in a way that is not formally correct but seems likely to simplify the exposition or suggest the correct intuition.
abuser: One who abuses someone or something.
abusive: Prone to treat someone badly by coarse, insulting words or other maltreatment; vituperative; reproachful; scurrilous.
Being physically or emotionally injurious; characterized by repeated violence or other abuse.
Wrongly used; perverted; misapplied; unjust; illegal.
abut: To touch by means of a mutual border, edge or end; to border on; to lie adjacent (to); to be contiguous (said of an area of land)
To border upon; be next to; abut on; be adjacent to.
To lean against on one end; to end on, of a part of a building or wall.
abutment: The point of junction between two things, in particular a support, that abuts.
The solid portion of a structure that supports the lateral pressure of an arch or vault.
A construction that supports the ends of a bridge; a structure that anchors the cables on a suspension bridge.
The part of a valley or canyon wall against which a dam is constructed.
abuttal: To describe a piece of land in terms of its abuttals.
The butting or boundary of land, particularly at the end; buttals.
abuzz: Characterized by a high level of activity or gossip; in a buzz (“feeling or rush of energy or excitement”), buzzing.
abwehr: German military intelligence service for the Reichswehr and Wehrmacht (1920-1945).
The military intelligence service of the German Weimar Republic and Third Reich, from 1920 to 1944 or 1945.
abydos: An ancient city in Egypt with archaeological interest.
An ancient city of Mysia in northwest Asia Minor in modern Turkey, on the Hellespont.
abysmally: Very; incredibly; profoundly; to an extreme degree; dreadfully.
abyssal blue: Of a dark shade of blue.
abyssal fish: Any fish that lives below a depth of 2000 meters.
abyssal plain: A large expanse of very flat and smooth ocean floor, usually found at depths of 4,600 to 5,500 meters (15,000 to 18,000 feet).
abyssal rock: An igneous rock that crystallized at considerable depth in the crust; plutonic rock.
abyssal zone: The oceanic realm consisting of the deep ocean, typified by a dearth of plant life, and plentiful carnivorous animals that are able to withstand extreme pressure.
abyssinian: Of or pertaining to Ethiopia or its inhabitants; Ethiopian.
A short-haired domestic cat descended from the cats of ancient Egypt, making it one of the oldest breeds in the world.
A member of the Abyssinian Church.
acacia avenue: A placeholder name for a residential street.
An archetypal middle-class suburban residential street.
acacia tit: Melaniparus thruppi, a small bird of the tit family Paridae
academy: An institution for the study of higher learning; a college or a university; typically a private school.
academic: Belonging to the school or philosophy of Plato.
academe: A senior member of the staff at an institution of higher learning; pedant.
The garden in Athens where the academics met.
An academy; a place of learning.
The scholarly life, environment, or community.
academia: The scientific and cultural community engaged in higher education and research, taken as a whole.
Continuous study at higher education institutions; scholarship.
academic bulimia: An approach to test-taking in which information is memorized shortly before the test and then quickly forgotten afterwards.
academic costume: An outfit, typically consisting of a cap and gown, worn by academics on special occasions such as graduation.
academic freedom: The right to teach, learn, and (communicate) research freely without unreasonable interference from authority, or fear of reprisal.
academic institution: An educational institution, dedicated to higher education and research, that grants academic degrees.
An educational institution, dedicated to teaching and/or research.
academic quarter: The traditional fifteen-minutes discrepancy between the time a university lecture nominally will start (according to schedule) and the time it actually starts, used in some educational institutions.
academic question: A question that is only of interest to academic scholars; a question of no practical importance.
academical: Pertaining to a university or other form of higher education.
Academic dress, consisting of a cap and gown.
Belonging to the school of Plato; believing in Plato's philosophy; sceptical .
academically: In an academic style or way; from an academic perspective.
academically disadvantaged: Uneducated; lacking access to an education; lacking resources required to receive an education.
academicism: The doctrines of Plato's academy; specifically the skeptical doctrines of the later academy stating that nothing can be known; a tenet of the Academic philosophy; state of being Academic.
A mannerism or mode peculiar to an academy.
academism: The doctrines of Plato's academy; specifically the skeptical doctrines of the later academy stating that nothing can be known; a tenet of the Academic philosophy; state of being Academic.
academy award: An award in any of various fields related to moviemaking, most prominently acting, generally awarded at a televised gala to winners who then speak; commonly used to indicate a person has been lying with great skill.
academy awards: The ceremony at which Academy Award winners are announced and receive their prizes.
acadia: Colony of New France in northeastern North America.

A former French colony in North America in the 17th and early 18th centuries, spanning over what are now the Maritime provinces of eastern Canada (Nova Scotia, New Brunswick and Prince Edward Island) and part of the state of Maine in the United States.
Acadia National Park, a national park in Maine.
A parish in southern Louisiana, first settled by some Acadian exiles then by mostly Franco-Americans: see Acadia Parish.
